questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had been to Italy before and wanted to get to know the language and culture better.

questions.answer: I rented through Novocento Case and it was good but a bit expensive

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's expensive, more than in Copenhagen

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Quite simple

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always email the office at the university and they very friendly and helpful

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Please note that there are differences between which subjects trigger ects points at your host and home university. There can be discrepancies, which I experienced and it was a bit of a headache when I had to start a new subject late in the process.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I could almost only enroll in a master's degree in English, even though I was doing my bachelor's. It was challenging because I had electives from other fields of study, so the other students had a lot of background knowledge that I had to familiarize myself with. But in return, I learned a lot.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: it is more about memorization. In Denmark we learn to use knowledge and put it in context and have a critical reflection ourselves. In my opinion, in Italy it was more about learning theories by heart.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: contemporary English literature, english business communication, intellectual history in the 19th century

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: contemporary english literature. really good teacher! also english business communication, because the teacher was nice and to improve one's english (not so much the business aspect)

questions.answer: not so many to my knowledge

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: take the flixbus to other cities and explore the food culture !

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: see the Duomo, go to museums and get restaurant recommendations

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fine and very helpful if you have some classmates to help each other

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No I'm afraid that I found it a bit hard

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: You have to get used to the relationship between student and teacher. You don't address your teacher by their first name and there is generally a more formal and submissive approach to the teacher, where in Denmark you are considered more on the same wavelength.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food culture! And also the people is very passionate and positive! Beautiful architecture too

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It is important to be dressed appropriately. The style is not as relaxed and free as in Copenhagen. People will look at you strangely, for example if you wear flip-flops in the summer in the city and not only when you are out swimming.

If you are there in the spring it will be hot! it is an interesting experience when you are not used to the warm climate. but it is also a lot about the apartment and its location.

The teaching method is different, so it calls for some adjustment

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I experienced some disagreements with a teacher, which I have never experienced before. It was a bit unfortunate, but something like that can probably also happen due to cultural differences.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in another country for a longer period of time and experiencing another culture up close was enriching, both because I got to know the new culture well, but it also put my life back home in perspective and made me appreciate certain things and get to know myself better.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Inconsistencies between my host university and home university regarding credit transfer of a subject. And problems with a teacher I found a bit unpleasant and harsh in his assessment. He failed me in a subject and I didn't understand why and when I tried to have a dialogue with him he was quite unpleasant. You have to be prepared that there can be some hassle with the practicalities and university rules when you are on exchange because things are different than at home. But you also learn from it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
